summary: Broom Service is a bluffing-driven role-selection game where players choose bold or timid versions of witch and druid roles to deliver potions. The simultaneous reveal creates constant tension as bold actions are more powerful but can be blocked by other bold players.
praised: Clever push-your-luck role selection with real bluffing tension
Quick to teach and plays fast
Fun simultaneous-reveal moments that spark table talk
criticised: Can feel swingy or luck-driven in outcomes
Round structure can feel repetitive over 7 rounds

interaction.detail: Players secretly choose roles that are revealed simultaneously, and bold actions get blocked if multiple players choose the same bold role, directly punishing predictable play. The delivery board and potions are shared, while each player's chosen cards stay hidden until reveal.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Points come mainly from delivering potions to matching-colored houses, with a secondary bonus for houses you've built yourself.
scoring.how_you_win: Each round, secretly choose bold or timid versions of witch, druid, and gatherer roles to collect and fly potions across the map, delivering them to matching-colored houses for points; whoever has the most delivery points after seven rounds wins.
